capabilities.name: Multi-node routing and port transfer
capabilities.note: Phase 5 seal: the native routing acceptor implements the non-broker ipcz Router state machine (terminal/proxy routers, decaying links, sequenced parcel queues, closure propagation, WithLocalPeer deserialization, SerializeNewRouterAndConfigureProxy + BeginProxyingToNewRouter, AcceptBypassLink, StopProxying teardown, RouterLinkState TryLock/SetSideStable, and the full bridge chain: MergeRoute-equivalent setup, bridge-aware Flush/StopProxyingToLocalPeer/AcceptRouteClosureFrom, and MaybeStartBridgeBypass/StartBridgeBypassFromLocalPeer for all three cases). The acceptor-initiated bridge bypass is reproduced message-for-message (BypassPeerWithLink(1->14), FlushRouter(14), StopProxyingToLocalPeer(14, 0); transfer-back on sublink 15, descriptor new=16) and the official broker's event stream is byte-identical to the oracle-acceptor baseline; both processes exit 0. Not yet implemented: multi-node graphs, multi-subparcel/split parcels, node loss beyond the single link, and the RequestMemory/ProvideMemory round trip (implemented and unit-tested, but its only reachable trigger in this epoch — RouterLinkState pool exhaustion — requires the proxy-bypass machinery, the next gate). Reproduce: scripts/run_routing_court.sh

capabilities.name: Parcel-fragment allocation and free-list reuse (memory court)
capabilities.note: Phase 5 memory court: the native memory-acceptor's parcel-fragment allocation, 256-byte pool exhaustion (inline fallback), and LIFO free-list reuse are byte-observable on the acceptor->broker wire and match the baseline byte-for-byte (modulo node names and per-link sequence numbers); the broker's event streams are byte-identical. The pinned mojo embedder sets IPCZ_MEMORY_FIXED_PARCEL_CAPACITY (crbug.com/40876289), disabling parcel-data expansion, so the RequestMemory/ProvideMemory/AddBlockBuffer round trip is implemented and unit-tested but not differentially triggered in this epoch (its only reachable trigger is RouterLinkState pool exhaustion, which requires the proxy-bypass machinery). Reproduce: scripts/run_memory_court.sh

capabilities.name: Block-capacity exhaustion: AddBlockBuffer receive side (exhaustion court)
capabilities.note: Phase 5 exhaustion court: 1486 held portal transfers exhaust the primary buffer's 64-byte RouterLinkState pool; the broker shares a new 64 KiB block buffer via AddBlockBuffer; the native exhaust-acceptor adopts it and resolves the remaining transfers' link states from it (cross-buffer fragment resolution), handles the exhausted-pool proxy transfer and the route migrations, and delivers the complete route sequence (rseq 0..1485); the broker's event streams are byte-identical. Documented residual: the exhaustion point differs between the runs (the native retains decayed RouterLinkState blocks - the free-timing boundary shared with the routing court). Reproduce: scripts/run_exhaust_court.sh
